reported_quantity: % of alcohol-industry/SAPRO webpages discussing cardiovascular impacts that state alcohol is associated with a reduced risk of at least one cardiovascular condition (a claim the authors judge to misrepresent the evidence)
denominator: 12 of the 18 alcohol-industry/SAPRO sources whose sampled webpages refer specifically to the cardiovascular impacts of drinking
misinfo_definition: "AI-funded health organizations mis-represent the evidence on cardiovascular effects of moderate alcohol consumption"; "the information they provide has the characteristics of other unhealthy commodity industry-funded misinformation, and significantly misrepresents the evidence"

reported_quantity: % of respondents who report ever sharing a political news story online that they thought AT THE TIME was made up (Study 1)
denominator: 507 US adult social media users drawn from the Prolific research panel (Study 1)
misinfo_definition: "false or manipulated political material which is likely to mislead audiences"

reported_quantity: % of survey respondents NOT in favour of the statement that the information they received about the Russo-Ukrainian war was reliable (i.e. perceiving the war information they received as unreliable, incl. neutral responses)
denominator: 840 Greek adults who completed an online questionnaire distributed nationwide via email and social media (approx. 3,000 recipients contacted)
misinfo_definition: "There is likely to be both much misinformation (unintentional dissemination of inaccurate information) and disinformation (inaccurate information intended to mislead) (Gilchrist 2016)."

reported_quantity: % of videos discoverable only with medical search terms ('cholecystectomy', 'appendectomy', 'cholecystitis', 'appendicitis') that contained misinformation
denominator: Videos in the 200-video sample discoverable only with medical search terms; the exact subset size is not reported
misinfo_definition: "A Likert scale from 1 to 5 was used to estimate the amount of patient education and of misinformation. This scale was based on the reviewer's perception of total patient education and misinformation."

reported_quantity: % of websites informing about antidepressant withdrawal effects that gave misleading or incorrect information about them
denominator: 28 of the 39 websites that informed patients about withdrawal effects caused by sudden cessation of antidepressants
misinfo_definition: Information that 'conflicted with the scientific evidence'; the conclusion calls it 'The widespread misinformation'

reported_quantity: % of included TikTok varicocele videos presenting inaccurate information
denominator: 36 English-language TikTok videos about varicoceles that met inclusion criteria, from the first 225 videos returned by TikTok's 'top' (engagement) sort for the keyword 'varicocele'
misinfo_definition: No formal definition; content is described as 'misinformation' / 'inaccurate information', judged against urological fact (correct examples given: dilation of the pampiniform plexus, incompetent valves, impaired sperm production).

reported_quantity: % of respondents who report ever sharing a political news story online that they later found out was made up (Study 2, replication sample)
denominator: 527 US adult social media users drawn from the Prolific research panel (Study 2)
misinfo_definition: "false or manipulated political material which is likely to mislead audiences"

reported_quantity: % of citations of influential CMN-function studies that were unsupported by the cited evidence, at the most recent point of the time series
denominator: All citations of the eleven influential CMN-function studies in the most recent year of the record; the full corpus screened was 1,083 citing papers
misinfo_definition: "We assigned a citation as supported if the evidence was strong for the statement or unsupported if the evidence was weak or absent, or if alternative interpretations, such as those described above, were consistent with the evidence."

reported_quantity: % of respondents who had heard the left-leaning conspiracy theory who reported seeing it on television
denominator: Respondents who had heard the left-leaning conspiracy theory (53% of the 2,765-person sample; unweighted n = 1,348)
misinfo_definition: "conspiracy theories—that is, attempts to explain the causes of events through secret plots by powerful actors"

reported_quantity: % of English-language YouTube LMWH self-injection videos containing information that may harm the person receiving the injection
denominator: 161 unique English-language YouTube videos retrieved with five LMWH-injection keywords
misinfo_definition: "Misleading Information: Videos that were judged by the reviewers here to contain misleading information included inaccurate information or videos that did not contain any information on LMWH injection administration."

reported_quantity: % of licensed medical practitioners who report that patients raised medical misinformation in a clinical encounter within the past year
denominator: 2,183 analysed responses from physicians and physician assistants licensed in North Carolina (2,889 unique responses received; 2,183 retained after removing largely incomplete responses and practitioners not currently practising in NC; response rate 8.9% of 24,571)
misinfo_definition: 'information that is factually inaccurate or not supported by current evidence-based medical literature and/or practices'

reported_quantity: % of respondents whose reported action on news they find suspicious is to share/forward it immediately
denominator: 869 Malaysian online respondents aged 18-59 (self-administered Google Form survey, mostly tertiary students)
misinfo_definition: "Fake news, defined as concocted content that copycat legitimate news, presented subtly to lure the public into believing it is legitimate"

reported_quantity: % of websites mentioning addiction that stated (incorrectly) that SSRIs are not addictive
denominator: 23 of the 39 websites that mentioned 'addiction' with reference to antidepressants
misinfo_definition: Information that 'conflicted with the scientific evidence'; the conclusion calls it 'The widespread misinformation'

reported_quantity: % of bone sarcoma hashtag posts coded as misinformation (clearly false or misleading/unverified)
denominator: 1,201 publicly accessible English-language Instagram posts sampled from ten bone sarcoma-related hashtags
misinfo_definition: "(a) clearly false, comprising direct factual errors contradicted by peer-reviewed literature (e.g., claims that specific supplements cure bone sarcoma); (b) misleading or unverified, comprising unsubstantiated assertions lacking any supporting evidence but not directly refuted"

reported_quantity: % of surveyed vaccinees who agreed they read/learned from social media and/or TV/radio that COVID-19 vaccines were not safe and effective, which delayed their vaccination
denominator: 157 adult residents of Magallanes, Cavite who appeared at the vaccination site and completed the online questionnaire (20.0% of the 784 people who showed up on the four survey days)
misinfo_definition: Misinformation: misleading or inaccurate information (Greenspan & Loftus, 2021); Fake News: false stories that appear to be news, spread on the internet or using other media

reported_quantity: % of respondents who report ever sharing a political news story online that they thought AT THE TIME was made up (Study 2, replication sample)
denominator: 527 US adult social media users drawn from the Prolific research panel (Study 2)
misinfo_definition: "false or manipulated political material which is likely to mislead audiences"

reported_quantity: % of YouTube channels in an Italian COVID-19 keyword video corpus that were labelled questionable (unreliable/misinformation sources)
denominator: 7,157 Italian YouTube channels that posted videos matching COVID-19 keywords (coronavirus, nCov, corona virus, corona-virus, covid, SARS-CoV) collected via the YouTube Data API
misinfo_definition: "A channel was labeled as questionable if it regularly produced unverified or false content, or was affiliated with news outlets that had repeatedly failed fact-checks conducted by independent organizations."

reported_quantity: % of the top 20 news sites posted in conservative subreddits with a MediaBiasFactCheck factual rating of 'mixed' or lower
denominator: the 20 most-posted news sites in the 6 conservative subreddits
misinfo_definition: Sites in “the NewsGuardTech’s database of sites ﬂagged for COVID-19 misinformation”, whose “ﬂagged content includ[es] myths such as that Sars-Cov-2 was stolen by Chinese spies from a Canadian lab, that 5G technology is linked to the spread of COVID-19”; source credibility separately from MediaBiasFactCheck factual ratings (very low to very high) and NewsGuard trust scores

reported_quantity: % of check-worthy COVID-19 tweets citing a news article whose claim is not actually supported by the cited article (deceptive support)
denominator: approximately 5,000 English-language COVID-19 tweets in the test split (5,257) that contain a check-worthy factual claim and link to one of 27 top-ranked news-agency domains
misinfo_definition: "Posts that cite a news article but present claims unsupported by the source are candidates for misinformation."

reported_quantity: % of practitioners reporting they 'often' or 'sometimes' encountered patient misinformation about vaccines
denominator: 2,100 practitioners answering the vaccine-misinformation frequency item
misinfo_definition: 'information that is factually inaccurate or not supported by current evidence-based medical literature and/or practices'

reported_quantity: % of posts in the two neutral subreddits (r/coronavirus, r/science) that linked to a site flagged for COVID-19 misinformation
denominator: COVID-19 link posts in r/coronavirus (738) and r/science (441), 1,179 posts before self-post filtering
misinfo_definition: Sites in “the NewsGuardTech’s database of sites ﬂagged for COVID-19 misinformation”, whose “ﬂagged content includ[es] myths such as that Sars-Cov-2 was stolen by Chinese spies from a Canadian lab, that 5G technology is linked to the spread of COVID-19”; source credibility separately from MediaBiasFactCheck factual ratings (very low to very high) and NewsGuard trust scores

reported_quantity: % of fact-checked claims about the Russo-Ukrainian conflict rated invalid (False, Miscaptioned or Outdated)
denominator: 128 Snopes fact-checking reports on the Russo-Ukrainian conflict published 24 February 2022 - 28 June 2023, retrieved with the search terms 'Russia AND Ukraine' and 'Ukraine AND war'
misinfo_definition: "fact-checking can be defined as 'the practice of systematically publishing assessments of the validity of claims made by public officials and institutions with an explicit attempt to identify whether a claim is factual'"; ratings: valid (True, Correct Attribution), invalid (False, Miscaptioned, Outdated), mixed

reported_quantity: % of PFP websites whose description of manual therapy was rated inaccurate/misleading against consensus statements
denominator: 40 unique websites offering information about patellofemoral pain, from the first 20 Google and Bing results for 'patellofemoral pain' and 'knee cap pain' (80 URLs, minus 30 duplicates, 6 not PFP-specific, 4 inactive)
misinfo_definition: Content rated as "(iii) Inaccurate/Misleading description" relative to the International Patellofemoral Pain Research Network expert consensus statements

reported_quantity: % of users with a defined commenting leaning who are misinformation-prone (at least 75% of their comments posted on questionable channels)
denominator: 313,680 commenting users with a defined leaning (96.8% of the 324,006 users in the corpus; 10,326 users with a leaning score between 0.25 and 0.75 are excluded as undefined)
misinfo_definition: "A channel was labeled as questionable if it regularly produced unverified or false content, or was affiliated with news outlets that had repeatedly failed fact-checks conducted by independent organizations."

reported_quantity: % of posts in conservative subreddits that linked to a site flagged for COVID-19 misinformation
denominator: COVID-19 link posts in the 6 conservative subreddits (AskThe_Donald 372, Conservative 561, DrainTheSwamp 548, Libertarian 575, redacted 154, tucker_carlson 153; 2,363 posts before self-post filtering)
misinfo_definition: Sites in “the NewsGuardTech’s database of sites ﬂagged for COVID-19 misinformation”, whose “ﬂagged content includ[es] myths such as that Sars-Cov-2 was stolen by Chinese spies from a Canadian lab, that 5G technology is linked to the spread of COVID-19”; source credibility separately from MediaBiasFactCheck factual ratings (very low to very high) and NewsGuard trust scores

reported_quantity: % of respondents in latent class 4 who report having ever shared a political news story online that they thought at the time was made up (intentional sharing)
denominator: 265 Polish active Facebook news users in latent class 4 ("The most SM literate users"); total sample 1,000 recruited from the largest Polish research panel
misinfo_definition: "For the purpose of this study, fake news is understood as partially or completely false information, intended to mislead the recipient, which may be intentionally and unintentionally disseminated by online news consumers"

reported_quantity: % of videos discoverable with colloquial search terms ('appendix surgery', 'gallbladder surgery') that contained misinformation
denominator: Videos in the 200-video sample discoverable with the colloquial search terms 'appendix surgery' or 'gallbladder surgery'; the exact subset size is not reported (search-criterion counts, which overlap across terms, are appendix surgery 50 and gallbladder surgery 67)
misinfo_definition: "A Likert scale from 1 to 5 was used to estimate the amount of patient education and of misinformation. This scale was based on the reviewer's perception of total patient education and misinformation."

reported_quantity: % of respondents in latent class 3 who report having ever shared a political news story online that they later found out was made up (unintentional sharing)
denominator: 126 Polish active Facebook news users in latent class 3 ("The least SM literate users with high self-esteem"); total sample 1,000 recruited from the largest Polish research panel
misinfo_definition: "For the purpose of this study, fake news is understood as partially or completely false information, intended to mislead the recipient, which may be intentionally and unintentionally disseminated by online news consumers"

reported_quantity: % of Microsoft Cortana responses to HPV vaccine queries containing at least one instance of misinformation
denominator: 61 analysable Cortana responses (Cortana provided between three and nine text or video results per query)
misinfo_definition: We defined misinformation as either deliberate or accidental promotion of previously disproved or unproven beliefs, attitudes, and behaviors.

reported_quantity: % of COVID-19 YouTube videos in the Italian corpus posted by channels labelled questionable
denominator: 30,436 Italian YouTube videos matching COVID-19 keywords, posted 01/12/2019-21/04/2020
misinfo_definition: "A channel was labeled as questionable if it regularly produced unverified or false content, or was affiliated with news outlets that had repeatedly failed fact-checks conducted by independent organizations."

reported_quantity: % of posts in liberal subreddits that linked to a site flagged for COVID-19 misinformation
denominator: COVID-19 link posts in the 6 liberal subreddits (EnoughTrumpSpam 430, Esist 362, Political_Revolution 495, politics 525, SandersForPresident 396, Socialism 518; 2,726 posts before self-post filtering)
misinfo_definition: Sites in “the NewsGuardTech’s database of sites ﬂagged for COVID-19 misinformation”, whose “ﬂagged content includ[es] myths such as that Sars-Cov-2 was stolen by Chinese spies from a Canadian lab, that 5G technology is linked to the spread of COVID-19”; source credibility separately from MediaBiasFactCheck factual ratings (very low to very high) and NewsGuard trust scores

reported_quantity: % of survey respondents who had heard the right-leaning conspiracy theory that the shooting was planned by Democratic operatives
denominator: 2,765 US adults, online nonprobability panel (PureSpectrum) with quotas for gender, race, age and region, poststratification-weighted to US Census benchmarks
misinfo_definition: "conspiracy theories—that is, attempts to explain the causes of events through secret plots by powerful actors"

reported_quantity: % of pelvic organ prolapse YouTube video transcripts rated as containing high misinformation (Likert >= 3 of 5) against IUGA/ICS treatment guidelines
denominator: 100 English-narrated YouTube videos on 'pelvic organ prolapse', the first 135 search results minus exclusions (not English n = 4, no text or audio n = 1, surgical procedure n = 8, longer than 10 minutes n = 22)
misinfo_definition: "Misinformation was evaluated using a likert scale (1 = no misinformation to 5 = high misinformation) by comparing content to accepted POP management recommendations from educational literature and an International Urogynecological Association (IUGA)/International Continence Society (ICS) joint report guidelines, as the reference measure"

reported_quantity: % of survey respondents who reported having shared COVID-19 misinformation since the outbreak (self-reported sharing or selection of at least one of 12 verified false items)
denominator: 1,317 Chinese adults recruited on the Credamo crowdsourcing platform (after excluding 44 attention-check failures)
misinfo_definition: "self-corrected debunking as the act of individuals who have previously shared misinformation voluntarily disseminating corrective information after realizing their mistakes"; the 12 items were "collected from Chinese mainstream media and were trending on Weibo" with debunkings "sourced from authoritative Chinese fact-checking websites, including Tencent Fact Check and Dingxiang Yisheng"

reported_quantity: % of respondents who say they came across information in the last month that they knew or learned was fake news
denominator: 745 US respondents completing both panel waves (n = 685 in the regression models)
misinfo_definition: "fake news" defined for respondents as "news that was produced in order to give false information"

reported_quantity: % of respondents in latent class 2 who report having ever shared a political news story online that they thought at the time was made up (intentional sharing)
denominator: 65 Polish active Facebook news users in latent class 2 ("The most educated users with SM literacy below average"); total sample 1,000 recruited from the largest Polish research panel
misinfo_definition: "For the purpose of this study, fake news is understood as partially or completely false information, intended to mislead the recipient, which may be intentionally and unintentionally disseminated by online news consumers"

reported_quantity: % of government resources on BC drug decriminalization that contained misleading content (technically accurate but distorting)
denominator: 98 government resources on BC's decriminalization policy
misinfo_definition: "misleading content is factually accurate information that is presented in a manner that creates confusion or distorts the surrounding context"

reported_quantity: % of sampled laser-refractive-surgery TikTok videos judged to contain potentially harmful misinformation
denominator: 240 English-language TikTok videos about LASIK, LASEK or SMILE with over 1000 views, sampled a fixed number per LRS hashtag in January 2025
misinfo_definition: "subjectively harmful misinformation as determined by the grader"

reported_quantity: % of alcohol-industry/SAPRO webpages mentioning the J-shaped curve that over-generalize that evidence to all adults or all cardiovascular disease
denominator: 10 alcohol-industry/SAPRO webpages that mention the J-shaped curve
misinfo_definition: "AI-funded health organizations mis-represent the evidence on cardiovascular effects of moderate alcohol consumption"; "the information they provide has the characteristics of other unhealthy commodity industry-funded misinformation, and significantly misrepresents the evidence"

reported_quantity: % of respondents who have ever knowingly spread a fake news item through any medium
denominator: 501 Spanish adults aged 18-25 interviewed online in the Netquest panel, quota-weighted to National Institute of Statistics proportions for sex, age, region and social class (sampling error +/-4.47%, 95% confidence)
misinfo_definition: fake news, that is, rumors, hoaxes, lies (questionnaire wording, Q3); the paper adopts the Ethical Journalism Network definition, 'information deliberately fabricated and published with the intention to deceive and mislead others into believing falsehoods or doubting verifiable facts'
